kicker: Cactus Whistle, from its own checkpoint

scenes.headline: How a 16.9 MB model turns speech into text
scenes.sub: Cactus Whistle: an audio encoder, a small decoder, two bits a weight.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rusk! Whistle is a speech recognizer in one small file, running on a phone's processor. Here's how it hears.

scenes.text: An encoder hears the whole clip once. A small decoder reads it at every layer, and the whole model is trained to survive 2 bits a weight.
scenes.say: The idea: an encoder hears the clip once, a small decoder reads it at every layer, and the model is trained to survive two bits a weight.

steps.say: Sound arrives at sixteen thousand samples a second and becomes eighty log mel energies every ten milliseconds.
Convolutions shrink that to one frame every eighty milliseconds. The encoder attends across the whole clip.
Its keys and values are computed once and held.
The decoder writes text piece by piece, reading that memory at every layer, shared by five beams.

scenes.title: How the decoder listens
scenes.text: x <- x + sigmoid(g) * attention(q, K, V)

parts.note: the text asks, the audio answers
parts.say: Each decoder layer asks the audio a question: text state as query, audio frames as keys and values.

parts.note: one gate per layer, wide open after training
parts.say: A learned gate scales the answer. In the shipped checkpoint, all eight are fully open.

scenes.title: Keyword biasing
scenes.say: Rare names lose to common spellings. Whistle fixes that during search.

items.say: You hand it the names your users say.
The engine builds one automaton tracking every name at once.
Each beam carries a place in it.
Matching beams get a boost. Too much, and names appear unsaid.

steps.say: Cactus's own drawing: the encoder on top, and below it the decoder, with its cross memory, gated cross attention and beam search.

scenes.title: FLEURS, seven languages
scenes.say: One check. On the multilingual average, the chart draws Whisper base at twenty-four point five. Its paper's table averages twenty-one, slightly ahead of Whistle.

scenes.text: The small file is real. It comes from training at 2 bits, not from a tiny network.
scenes.say: The small file is real. It comes mostly from training at two bits, not from shrinking the network.

recap: Encoder hears once, decoder reads always
scenes.say: Hear once, read at every layer, lift the names, and train it small.
